f.title: Apply the RMP Guidance to new drugs and follow-on biologics applied for on or after 1 April 2013
f.statement: The Guidance shall be applicable to new drugs and follow-on biologics for which approval applications are submitted on or after April 1, 2013; for generic drugs, the timing of application of the Guideline will be informed separately.
f.clause: Cover notification
f.applicability: New drugs and follow-on biologics; English translation by PMDA provided for reference only (the Japanese original prevails; the translation is not legally binding)
f.exceptions: Generic drugs: timing to be informed separately

f.title: Consider developing an RMP at new-drug, follow-on biologic and relevant generic applications, and on new post-marketing safety concerns
f.statement: Based on the Guidance, development of the RMP should be considered at the following milestones: submission of the approval application for new drugs (as defined in Article 14-4(1)(i) of the Pharmaceutical Affairs Law); submission of the approval application for follow-on biologics; submission of the approval application for generic versions of original drugs for which additional pharmacovigilance or additional risk minimisation activities ("additional actions") are being performed; and when new safety concerns have been identified in the post-marketing phase.
f.clause: 1.2 Scope
f.legal_basis: Pharmaceutical Affairs Law Art. 14-4(1)(i) (definition of new drugs)
f.applicability: Ethical drugs, including new drugs, follow-on biologics and generic drugs (PFSB/SD Notification No. 0411-1 / PFSB/ELD Notification No. 0411-2, 11 April 2012); English translation by PMDA provided for reference only (the Japanese original prevails; the translation is not legally binding)

rows.quote:
Based on this Guidance, development of the risk management plan should be
  considered at the following milestones:


     At the time of submission of approval application for new drugs (the term “new
      drugs” means new drugs as defined in Article 14-4, paragraph (1), item (i) of the
      Pharmaceutical Affairs Law [Law No. 145, 1960; hereinafter referred to as “the
      Law”]; the same shall apply hereinafter) ;
     At the time of submission of approval application for follow-on biologics;
                                                                                  6 / 17




    At the time of submission of approval application for generic drug versions of the
     original drugs for which additional pharmacovigilance activities or additional
     risk minimization activities (hereinafter referred to as “additional actions”) are
     being performed;
    At the time when new concerns regarding safety have been identified in the
     post-marketing phase.
rows.location: 1.2 Scope
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: passive 'should be considered'; the quote is a bulleted list with the page number '6 / 17' inside it; the actor is inferred. Below 90.

f.title: Identify the Safety Specification, develop the pharmacovigilance and risk minimisation plans (and efficacy plan if needed), and consolidate them into an RMP
f.statement: To promote proper use and maintain an appropriate risk-benefit balance, MAHs and applicants should identify the Safety Specification (section 3), develop a Pharmacovigilance Plan (section 4) and a Risk Minimization Plan (section 6) based on it, develop a plan for post-marketing survey/study on efficacy (section 5) when necessary, and then prepare a Risk Management Plan by consolidating these plans.
f.clause: 2.1 Development of Risk Management Plan
f.applicability: Ethical drugs, including new drugs, follow-on biologics and generic drugs (PFSB/SD Notification No. 0411-1 / PFSB/ELD Notification No. 0411-2, 11 April 2012); English translation by PMDA provided for reference only (the Japanese original prevails; the translation is not legally binding)

rows.quote:
In order to always promote proper use of drugs and maintain an appropriate
 risk-benefit balance, MAHs and applicants for marketing authorization should
 identify the Safety Specification of drugs as described in section 3, and develop a
 Pharmacovigilance Plan as described in section 4 and a Risk Minimization Plan as
 described in section 6 based on the identified Safety Specification. When necessary,
 they should also develop a plan for post-marketing survey/study on efficacy as
 described in section 5. The MAHs and applicants for marketing authorization should
 then prepare a Risk Management Plan by consolidating these plans.
rows.location: 2.1 Development of Risk Management Plan
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: verified: 'should', MAHs and applicants as actors, and the whole sequence of plans is in the quote.

f.title: Consider additional actions together with routine practices and state in the RMP whether they are taken, with reasons and methods
f.statement: When developing an RMP, the necessity of additional actions should be considered at the same time as routine pharmacovigilance and routine risk minimisation practices depending on the Safety Specification, and the RMP should clearly describe whether these actions are taken or not, together with the reasons and the methods.
f.clause: 2.2 Points to Consider in Development of Risk Management Plan
f.applicability: Ethical drugs, including new drugs, follow-on biologics and generic drugs (PFSB/SD Notification No. 0411-1 / PFSB/ELD Notification No. 0411-2, 11 April 2012); English translation by PMDA provided for reference only (the Japanese original prevails; the translation is not legally binding)

When developing a Risk Management Plan, the necessity of additional actions should

 taken or not, together with the reasons and the methods.
rows.location: 2.2 Points to Consider in Development of Risk Management Plan
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: passive 'should' and the actor is not named in the quote (inferred). Below 90.

f.title: Prepare the RMP consistently with the contents of the review reports
f.statement: Because the validity of the RMP is assessed during approval review, the RMP should be prepared so that it is consistent with the contents of the review reports.
f.clause: 2.2 Points to Consider in Development of Risk Management Plan
f.applicability: Ethical drugs, including new drugs, follow-on biologics and generic drugs (PFSB/SD Notification No. 0411-1 / PFSB/ELD Notification No. 0411-2, 11 April 2012); English translation by PMDA provided for reference only (the Japanese original prevails; the translation is not legally binding)

rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: passive 'should' and the actor is not named in the quote (inferred). Below 90.

f.title: Perform routine pharmacovigilance (ADR and infection reporting) and routine risk minimisation even when no additional actions are needed
f.statement: Even for drugs for which additional actions have been judged unnecessary, routine pharmacovigilance practices (including collection and reporting of information on ADRs and infections) as stipulated in Article 77-4(2) of the Law and routine risk minimisation practices (including provision of information through package inserts) must be appropriately performed.
f.clause: 2.2 Points to Consider in Development of Risk Management Plan
f.applicability: Ethical drugs, including new drugs, follow-on biologics and generic drugs (PFSB/SD Notification No. 0411-1 / PFSB/ELD Notification No. 0411-2, 11 April 2012); English translation by PMDA provided for reference only (the Japanese original prevails; the translation is not legally binding)

rows.quote:
It should be noted that, even for drugs for which additional actions have been judged
unnecessary as a result of considering the Risk Management Plan based on the Safety
Specification, routine pharmacovigilance practices (including collection and reporting
of information regarding ADRs and infections) as stipulated in Article 77-4,
paragraph (2) of the Law and routine risk minimization practices (including provision
of information through package inserts etc.) must be appropriately performed.
rows.location: 2.2 Points to Consider in Development of Risk Management Plan
rows.review_note: Review: Mandatory kept: 'must be appropriately performed' and the quote cites Pharmaceutical Affairs Law Art. 77-4(2) for routine pharmacovigilance. f.title: Set milestones for evaluating results or reporting to PMDA for each activity and describe them in the RMP
f.statement: When developing an RMP, milestones for evaluating results or for reporting to PMDA should be established for individual pharmacovigilance and risk minimisation activities and described activity by activity in the RMP.
f.clause: 2.3 Setting of Milestones in Risk Management Plan
f.applicability: Ethical drugs, including new drugs, follow-on biologics and generic drugs (PFSB/SD Notification No. 0411-1 / PFSB/ELD Notification No. 0411-2, 11 April 2012); English translation by PMDA provided for reference only (the Japanese original prevails; the translation is not legally binding)

rows.quote:
When developing a Risk Management Plan, the milestones for evaluating the results
or for reporting to the Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency (hereinafter
referred to the “PMDA”) should be established by individual pharmacovigilance
activities and risk minimization activities and be described on an activity-by-activity
basis in the Risk Management Plan.
rows.location: 2.3 Setting of Milestones in Risk Management Plan
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: passive 'should' and the actor is not named in the quote (inferred). Below 90.

f.title: Plan milestones so overall progress and each Safety Specification item can be managed
f.statement: The milestone plan should make it possible to manage the progress of overall activities and of individual Safety Specification items; for example, when one activity examines more than one item, a milestone for evaluation or reporting of each item should be established so that each target is achieved at an appropriate time point.
f.clause: 2.3 Setting of Milestones in Risk Management Plan
f.applicability: Ethical drugs, including new drugs, follow-on biologics and generic drugs (PFSB/SD Notification No. 0411-1 / PFSB/ELD Notification No. 0411-2, 11 April 2012); English translation by PMDA provided for reference only (the Japanese original prevails; the translation is not legally binding)

rows.quote:
Although the milestones are to be established individually for pharmacovigilance
activities and risk minimization activities, this plan of milestones should be the one
that makes the management of the progress of overall activities and the progress of
individual items of the Safety Specifications possible; for example, when examining
more than one item of the Safety Specification in one activity, a milestone for
evaluation or reporting of each item of Safety Specification should be established so
that the target of each item of the Safety Specification be achieved at an appropriate
time point.
rows.location: 2.3 Setting of Milestones in Risk Management Plan
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: passive 'should' and the actor is not named in the quote (inferred). Below 90.

f.statement: Even after the RMP has been developed, it should be reviewed depending on the post-marketing situation, and its contents should be revised to maintain an appropriate benefit-risk balance of the drug.
f.clause: 2.4 Review of Risk Management Plan
f.applicability: Ethical drugs, including new drugs, follow-on biologics and generic drugs (PFSB/SD Notification No. 0411-1 / PFSB/ELD Notification No. 0411-2, 11 April 2012); English translation by PMDA provided for reference only (the Japanese original prevails; the translation is not legally binding)

f.clause: 2.4 Review of Risk Management Plan
f.applicability: Ethical drugs, including new drugs, follow-on biologics and generic drugs (PFSB/SD Notification No. 0411-1 / PFSB/ELD Notification No. 0411-2, 11 April 2012); English translation by PMDA provided for reference only (the Japanese original prevails; the translation is not legally binding)

f.title: Conduct Early Post-marketing Phase Vigilance as additional pharmacovigilance where necessary
f.statement: Because rare and serious ADRs of new drugs may be observed early after marketing, it is important that MAHs provide medical institutions with correct information and alerts, promote proper use, collect serious ADR information quickly, take necessary safety measures and minimise health hazards; therefore, if necessary, Early Post-marketing Phase Vigilance is required as an additional pharmacovigilance activity.
f.clause: 4.2 Additional Pharmacovigilance Activities
f.applicability: New drugs; English translation by PMDA provided for reference only (the Japanese original prevails; the translation is not legally binding)
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Local PV interfaces

    quickly, take necessary safety measures, and minimize health hazards from the

f.title: Consider additional pharmacovigilance where high background incidence makes ADR attribution difficult

the same time, the benefit-risk balance of the drug should also be evaluated and
considered based on the information obtained from individual activities conducted
according to the Risk Management Plan.
rows.location: 7. Evaluation of the Risk Management Plan and Report to the PMDA
rows.review_note: Review: quote extended to include the benefit-risk sentence ('At the same time, the benefit-risk balance ... should also be evaluated and considered ...'), which the statement already contained but the quote did not prove. Double-check: passive 'should' and the actor is not named in the quote (inferred). Below 90.

f.title: Report the RMP evaluation summary with periodic safety reports during re-examination; otherwise at the timing set in the RMP
f.statement: For new drugs in the re-examination period, a summary of the evaluation should be reported at the time of submitting the periodic safety reports specified in Article 63 of the Enforcement Regulations (reports under Article 14-4(6) or the first half of Article 14-5(2) of the Law); for other drugs, the timing of reporting should be described in the RMP depending on the additional actions.
f.clause: 7. Evaluation of the Risk Management Plan and Report to the PMDA
f.legal_basis: Enforcement Regulations Art. 63; Pharmaceutical Affairs Law Art. 14-4(6), Art. 14-5(2)
f.applicability: Ethical drugs, including new drugs, follow-on biologics and generic drugs (PFSB/SD Notification No. 0411-1 / PFSB/ELD Notification No. 0411-2, 11 April 2012); English translation by PMDA provided for reference only (the Japanese original prevails; the translation is not legally binding)

rows.deadline: With the periodic safety reports (new drugs in re-examination); otherwise at the timing stated in the RMP
rows.quote:
As for new drugs which are in the re-examination period, a summary of the contents of
evaluation should be reported at the time of submitting periodic safety reports as
specified in Article 63 of the Enforcement Regulations (Ordinance of the Ministry of
Health and Welfare No.1, 1961) regarding reports stipulated in Article 14-4, paragraph
(6) or in the first half of Article 14-5, paragraph (2) of the Law. As for other drugs, the
timing of reporting should be described in the Risk Management Plan depending on the
contents of the additional actions.
rows.location: 7. Evaluation of the Risk Management Plan and Report to the PMDA
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Recommended is right: Enforcement Regulations Art. 63 is cited for the periodic safety report vehicle, not for this summary duty. passive 'should' and the actor is not named in the quote (inferred). Below 90.

f.title: Report RMP review results with the evaluation report; consult PMDA beforehand on plan changes as needed
f.statement: The review results of the RMP should be reported together with the evaluation report; if there are changes in the plan, MAHs should consult PMDA beforehand, as necessary.
f.clause: 7. Evaluation of the Risk Management Plan and Report to the PMDA
f.applicability: Ethical drugs, including new drugs, follow-on biologics and generic drugs (PFSB/SD Notification No. 0411-1 / PFSB/ELD Notification No. 0411-2, 11 April 2012); English translation by PMDA provided for reference only (the Japanese original prevails; the translation is not legally binding)

rows.quote:
The review results of the Risk Management Plan should also be reported together with
the above report. If there are changes in the plan, MAHs should preliminarily consult
with the PMDA, as necessary.
rows.location: 7. Evaluation of the Risk Management Plan and Report to the PMDA
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: the second sentence names the MAH ('should preliminarily consult'), but the first is passive, so the actor is inferred. Below 90.
